title: Daimler AG v. Bauman (2014)
summary: A corporation is at home, and so subject to general jurisdiction, in its place of incorporation and principal place of business and only in an exceptional case elsewhere; even attributing Mercedes-Benz USA’s substantial California sales to Daimler, judged against the company’s worldwide operations, did not make Daimler at home in California for claims about conduct in Argentina.
notes:
Do not turn this into a numerical percentage rule. The Court did not hold that a company is immune wherever its forum sales represent a small proportion of worldwide business.

Procedural history: the Northern District of California dismissed for want of personal jurisdiction; a Ninth Circuit panel first affirmed, then on rehearing reversed and upheld jurisdiction (with en banc rehearing denied); the Supreme Court (Ginsburg, J.) reversed the Ninth Circuit.

Rule statement: a corporation is 'at home' for general jurisdiction in its place of incorporation and its principal place of business, and only in an exceptional case elsewhere; the plaintiffs were Argentine residents suing over Mercedes-Benz Argentina's alleged collaboration with state security forces during the 'Dirty War'.

sections.Parties: Twenty-two residents of Argentina sued DaimlerChrysler Aktiengesellschaft, later Daimler AG, a German company headquartered in Stuttgart; they were the respondents and Daimler the petitioner. They sought to hold Daimler responsible for the conduct of Mercedes-Benz Argentina, a subsidiary, while relying for forum contacts on a different indirect subsidiary, Mercedes-Benz USA, LLC (MBUSA), a Delaware company with its principal place of business in New Jersey. Daimler was the sole corporate defendant named in the operative complaint.
sections.Material Facts: The plaintiffs alleged that Mercedes-Benz Argentina collaborated with Argentine security forces during the 1976–1983 “Dirty War” to kidnap, detain, torture and kill workers and their relatives, and they pleaded claims under the Alien Tort Statute, the Torture Victim Protection Act and California and Argentine law. None of the conduct, victims or perpetrators had any California connection. MBUSA imported Daimler vehicles from Germany and distributed them to independent dealers; it had a regional office, a vehicle preparation center and a classic-car center in California, where its sales were about 2.4 percent of Daimler’s worldwide total. The distributor agreement called MBUSA an independent contractor buying and selling for its own account with no authority to bind Daimler. The plaintiffs nevertheless argued that MBUSA was Daimler’s agent because its distribution work was essential to Daimler’s business.
sections.Procedural History: The plaintiffs filed in the Northern District of California in 2004. After jurisdictional discovery on the agency theory the district court dismissed, finding Daimler’s own contacts insufficient and declining to attribute MBUSA’s. A Ninth Circuit panel affirmed in 2009 with Judge Reinhardt dissenting, then on rehearing withdrew that opinion and, in an opinion by Reinhardt, 644 F.3d 909 (2011), treated MBUSA as Daimler’s agent because its services were so important that Daimler would perform them itself if MBUSA did not; rehearing en banc was denied over eight dissents. In the Supreme Court the plaintiffs did not pursue specific jurisdiction, alter ego or Daimler’s own contacts, and Daimler had not disputed that MBUSA itself was subject to general jurisdiction in California. The Court therefore assumed both that MBUSA was at home there and that its contacts could be attributed to Daimler, and reversed.
sections.Issue: May California exercise general jurisdiction over a German parent corporation for alleged misconduct in Argentina because an American subsidiary conducts substantial business in California, even assuming that the subsidiary’s contacts are attributable to the parent? Is substantial, continuous local business enough to make the parent answerable there on every claim?
sections.Holding: No. Justice Ginsburg wrote for eight Justices; Justice Sotomayor concurred in the judgment only. General jurisdiction ordinarily exists over a corporation in its state of incorporation and principal place of business, and another forum qualifies only in an exceptional case where the corporation’s operations there are so substantial and of such a nature as to render it at home. A substantial volume of business, considered in isolation, is insufficient; the assessment considers the corporation’s activities in their entirety, nationwide and worldwide. Even crediting all of MBUSA’s California contacts to Daimler, Daimler was not at home in California.
sections.Reasoning: The Ninth Circuit’s agency formulation was too broad: almost any subsidiary does work important enough that the parent would have to find another way to do it, so the test would expose a parent to general jurisdiction wherever an affiliate operated. The Court did not need to settle every attribution theory, because even the assumed attribution failed. The at-home standard gives all-purpose jurisdiction a definite scope: incorporation and principal place of business are readily ascertainable places where a company can anticipate suit on any claim, while Perkins shows that the list is not absolutely closed. California was a significant market, but so were many states and countries in which Daimler sold cars; treating every substantial market as a home would destroy predictability and restore jurisdiction over unrelated claims everywhere a large enterprise does business. The Court announced no percentage threshold; the character of the operation and its place in the whole business matter together. The international setting reinforced the point, since foreign plaintiffs sought to litigate foreign conduct through a distribution link, though the holding rested on the absence of an at-home relationship.

learning.why: The corporation’s California business did not support all-purpose jurisdiction over claims concerning alleged abuses in Argentina.

topics.general-jurisdiction: Substantial sales alone did not make California a home for an international enterprise. The global character of the enterprise informed whether local operations were exceptional enough to support all-purpose jurisdiction.
topics.cp-personal-jurisdiction: Even assuming the subsidiary’s contacts could be attributed to Daimler, the forum was not a corporate home.

learning.separateOpinions: Justice Sotomayor would have assumed the contacts sufficient and held the exercise of jurisdiction unreasonable given the foreign plaintiffs, German defendant, Argentine events and an available foreign forum. She objected that the Court decided a question not developed below after Daimler had conceded the sufficiency of MBUSA’s contacts, and that comparing forum contacts with a company’s operations elsewhere lets a larger corporation escape jurisdiction that the same local activity would support against a smaller one.
